reading.body:
ORNY1 sits on 23 acres near the New Jersey border, roughly 22 miles from Manhattan, with 232,000 square feet of built space and planned expansion to 462,000 square feet. The operator publishes 12 MW on site today and a provisioned target of 24 MW under N+2 redundancy, with substation capacity for up to 50 MW total. These figures are stated without a single unambiguous current operating critical IT load, so the campus's present power draw remains unclear from published data.

Assuming 40 kW per rack at AI training density, the operator's stated 24 MW provisioned capacity would support roughly 600 racks; assuming 400 W per accelerator, this could house roughly 60,000 GPUs or equivalent silicon. The facility qualifies for high density cabinets of 10 kW and above, and has access to 12 network providers. The substation capacity ceiling of 50 MW suggests the site is engineered for potential growth well beyond its current provision.

New York has 31 mapped data center facilities, of which only one other publishes a megawatt figure. ORNY1 ranks second in the state by published capacity among facilities on record, though the state total is only 3 MW in published figures. This campus represents one of the only transparent capacity statements in its region and is the larger of two published sites in New York.
